figures.title: The sliding window keeps only the last W keys in each row
figures.caption: With W = 4, each query scores only the four most recent keys including itself; earlier keys are masked out of the softmax and never read. The band slides down one row per token, so the work per token is W rather than n. At n = 131,072 and W = 4,096 the windowed path computes 536,870,912 pairs against 8,589,869,056 for full causal attention, 16x fewer.
figures.alt: A ten-by-ten mask grid. Row i has a 1 in columns i minus 3 through i and blank cells elsewhere, so the ones form a diagonal band that slides right as rows go down. The last row is highlighted and shows ones in columns 6 through 9. Blank cells are masked and never enter the softmax denominator.

data.note: Schematic 10 x 10 grid with W = 4. In the deployment W = 4,096; the band has 4,096 cells per row and the mask is applied tile by tile.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to slide the W = 4,096 band down the causal triangle.

steps.label: Each token attends only to the W = 4,096 positions ending at itself, so the first rows score every key they have.
The band slides down one row per token: row i keeps keys i - W + 1 through i and masks everything older.

Every row still scores at most W keys, so at n = 131,072 the window costs 131,072 x 4,096 = 536,870,912 pairs against 131,072 x 131,073 / 2 = 8,589,869,056 for full causal: about 16x fewer, and linear in n.

figures.title: Three patterns and what each costs
figures.caption: Full causal attention computes 8,589,869,056 pairs at n = 131,072. A sliding window of 4,096 computes 536,870,912 pairs, 16x fewer, and after 32 layers reaches 131,041 positions. Dilation 2 covers 8,191 positions with the same 4,096 scores per query; a hybrid of 16 full and 16 local layers costs 51.6 percent of an all-full stack.
figures.alt: Three aligned panels. Full causal lists 8,589,869,056 pairs at n = 131,072, every query reading every earlier key, with cost growing as n squared. The sliding window with W = 4,096 lists 536,870,912 pairs, 16 times fewer, a receptive field of 131,041 after 32 layers, and a cache holding only the last W positions. Dilated and global lists dilation 2 covering 8,191 positions with 4,096 scores, global tokens attended by every token, and a 16-full-plus-16-local hybrid at 51.6 percent of full cost.

panels.title: Full causal vs sliding window
panels.note: Full cost grows with n squared; the window costs W per token. The path back to position 1 is indirect, carried through 32 layers of averaging.

panels.title: Dilated, global, hybrid
items: global tokens attend to and are attended by every token
16 full + 16 local layers = 51.6% of full cost
panels.note: A full layer gives every token a direct edge; a local layer does not. That difference is what retrieval tests measure.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to price full attention against the sparse patterns built on it.

steps.label: Full causal attention at n = 131,072 costs 131,072 x 131,073 / 2 = 8,589,869,056 pairs.
A window of W = 4,096 costs at most 131,072 x 4,096 = 536,870,912 pairs, 16x fewer, and after L = 32 layers the receptive field is L(W - 1) + 1 = 32 x 4,095 + 1 = 131,041 positions.
Dilation 2 lets 4,096 scores cover 8,191 positions, global tokens attend to and are attended by every token, and 16 full plus 16 local layers cost 51.6% of 32 full layers.

figures.title: A rolling cache holds W positions, not the whole context
figures.caption: Mistral 7B's cache costs 128 KiB per token: 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 dimensions x 2 for K and V x 2 bytes. A 4,096-token window needs 512 MiB per stream, where holding 65,536 positions would need 8 GiB and a full 131,072-token prompt 16 GiB. The last two bars are 128 KiB multiplied by the position count, not separately measured sizes.
figures.alt: Three horizontal bars of cache size per stream. The rolling window of 4,096 positions is 512 MiB. A full cache over one stream's 65,536-position share is 8 GiB. A full cache over a 131,072-token prompt is 16 GiB.

data.note: 128 KiB per token = 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 (K/V) x 2 bytes. The rolling buffer writes token i to slot i mod W; position ids stay absolute so the mask still knows the true distance.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to price a rolling window against a cache that holds the whole prompt.

steps.label: Mistral 7B's fp16 cache is 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 dims x 2 for K/V x 2 bytes = 128 KiB per token.
A rolling buffer holds only W = 4,096 positions, so 4,096 x 128 KiB = 512 MiB per stream, whatever the prompt length.
A cache holding every position instead would pay 65,536 x 128 KiB = 8 GiB, and a full 131,072-token prompt 131,072 x 128 KiB = 16 GiB: 32x the window's footprint.
